items.title: War-related pollution: who pays?
points: Several international conventions establish strict shipowner liability backed by compulsory insurance.

These include the 1992 International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage (CLC), the 2001 International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage (the Bunkers Convention) and the Nairobi International Convention on the…
However, these conventions also contain exceptions to shipowner liability for certain war-related events.
Under the 2001 Bunkers Convention, for example, the shipowner is not liable if it proves that the pollution damage resulted from an act of war, hostilities, civil war or insurrection.
The same principle applies under CLC and under the Nairobi Convention.

The 2010 HNS Convention, which will enter into force on 29 November 2027, follows the same logic: strict shipowner liability backed by compulsory insurance, with exclusions for acts of war, hostilities, civil war and insurrection.

items.title: UK and EU aim to link emissions trading schemes by January 2028
points: The UK and EU have agreed to link their emissions trading systems, targeting 1 January 2028 for the arrangement to take effect alongside the UK’s planned expansion of carbon pricing to international shipping.

items.title: Meity revises ‘Made in India’ rules for govt IT hardware purchases
points: The ministry of electronics and information technology (Meity) has changed how laptops, desktops, servers and other IT hardware are judged as ‘Made in India’ for government purchases.

For a laptop, motherboard assembly counts for 15%, making the bare printed circuit board in India adds 10%, the chassis 10%, the battery pack and power adaptor 5% each, and final assembly and testing 5%.
In-house R&D done in India can account for 8% of the BoM.
Indian design or intellectual property can add another 10%.
Memory (RAM) and solid-state storage assembled on circuit boards in India count for 4% each.
That rises to 10% if the chips are also assembled, tested and packaged (ATMP) in India.
For servers, a board carrying the CPU and GPU together counts for 25%.
Where they are on separate boards, the CPU board counts for 15% and the GPU board for 10%.

items.title: Grounded Bulk Carrier MIRO G Successfully Refloated Off French Beach

The confirmation comes from Bentley chairman and CEO Frank-Steffen Walliser.

The performance-focused S produces up to 876 bhp and 1,350 Nm when launch control is active, according to the manufacturer.
Bentley currently sells fewer than 100 cars a year in India, according to the company’s recent comments.
The India–UK trade agreement came into force on 15 July 2026 and allows reduced import duties on qualifying British-made cars within set quotas.
The Torcal is expected here in 2027, well before EVs can benefit from those specific concessions under the current schedule.

items.title: Grounded bulker pulled free off French coast
points: Salvors have successfully refloated the 28,200 dwt bulk carrier Miro G, four days after the ship was driven onto a beach on France’s Atlantic coast.

The 2011-built, Malta-flagged bulker was pulled clear of the shoreline at Cap de l’Homy, near Lit-et-Mixe, on Tuesday afternoon by Les Abeilles International’s emergency response tug Abeille Bretagne.
The vessel is set to be towed north to Le Verdon, at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, according to Landes prefect Gilles Clavreul, who confirmed that no pollution had been detected.
The breakthrough followed days of preparations involving Dutch specialist SMIT Salvage, appointed by the shipowner, Les Abeilles International and experts from the French navy.

Salvors took advantage of improving sea conditions and a rising tide, pumping ballast water out of the 169-m-long bulker to reduce its draught before pulling it free using a 1,900-m high-strength synthetic towline.

items.title: Who is Lori Huang? How Jensen Huang’s wife holds the keys to Nvidia founder’s $109 billion fortune through family trusts
points: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's multibillion-dollar fortune is not entirely under his individual control.
While Jensen has built Nvidia into one of the world's most valuable technology companies, Lori's influence extends beyond the family.
She is a co-trustee of multiple trusts holding hundreds of millions of Nvidia shares and serves as president of the couple's philanthropic foundation, which reported assets of more than $9 billion.
According to a Wall Street Journal report, Jensen and Lori jointly control approximately 870 million Nvidia shares, worth more than $109 billion before Huang's return as CEO was announced.
The couple's ownership structure includes the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Living Trust, established in 1995, along with the Huang 2012 Irrevocable Trust and the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust.

The arrangement also came into focus after the couple transferred nearly 59 million Nvidia shares, valued at approximately $10.7 billion at the time, into the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust in March 2026.
The shares came from two grantor retained annuity trusts (GRATs) established by Jensen and Lori in 2016.

items.title: EnEarth takes control of Scottish carbon storage project

The transaction will transfer Storegga’s project interest and development responsibilities to EnEarth, together with the management team and staff currently working on Acorn.
The acquisition is expected to be completed before the end of 2026, subject to the necessary approvals.
Acorn is being developed around the St Fergus gas terminal near Peterhead and is designed to transport captured industrial carbon dioxide for permanent storage in depleted offshore gas reservoirs.
The project includes the Acorn and East Mey offshore storage areas, which have estimated combined storage capacity exceeding 140m tonnes of CO2.
Once developed, the facilities are expected to inject between 5m and 10m tonnes of CO2 annually into reservoirs approximately 2.5 km beneath the seabed.

1st privately built PSLV set for launch early next year: Isro chief
points: Isro Chairman V Narayanan announced the first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle is ready for launch.
This PSLV-N1 rocket is being developed by a consortium including L&T and HAL.
The government is promoting satellite launches in collaboration with startups, which have increased to over 440.
Narayanan emphasized the importance of building more space assets for communication and navigation.

items.title: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
points: In a recent family conversation about Sonia Gandhi's latest book, Rahul Gandhi accused the government of intentionally removing his father Rajiv Gandhi's security, suggesting it fostered the conditions for his assassination.
Following his exit from office in 1989, Rajiv's protection was significantly reduced.
Furthermore, Rahul is poised to address the political victimization and humiliation Sonia endured during her career.

items.title: Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review
points: Union home minister Amit Shah expressed that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor will only reopen after addressing prevailing security issues.
This corridor, which offers hassle-free access for pilgrims, was shut down following security alerts linked to Operation Sindoor.

Shah highlighted the need to keep national security discussions free from political influences, while also pointing out that the corridor's placement in Pakistan stemmed from Congress party oversights during partition.

items.title: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
points: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Maldives defense minister Hassan Rasheed discussed security cooperation at the Colombo Security Conclave.
This meeting marked the first high-level interaction between the two countries since President Mohamed Muizzu's recent visit to Pakistan.
During that visit, Maldives signed 20 agreements with Pakistan related to defense and maritime issues.
Additionally, Muizzu called for resuming the Saarc summit process to enhance regional cooperation.

items.title: PM Modi, Merz say India-EU FTA will unlock new opportunities
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently engaged in discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, focused on enhancing the India-Germany Strategic Partnership.
The conversation covered various critical areas including trade, investment, defence, and cutting-edge technologies, underscoring both nations’ dedication to global peace.
As they commemorate 75 years of diplomatic ties, they aim to bolster cooperation across essential sectors while sharing insights on regional issues of common interest.

items.title: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
points: The CII Banaras Biennale is set to commence on November 27, culminating on December 31.
This unique event aims to intertwine the ancient and modern art scenes, presenting the vibrant culture of Banaras.
Activities will unfold at numerous venues, including the distinguished Bharatiya Kala Bhavan.
By fostering partnerships between cultural institutions and industry, the Biennale aspires to spark rich dialogues, bridging diverse artistic expressions with their historical narratives.

items.title: Government may link motor insurance premiums to traffic violations
points: The road transport ministry is gearing up to introduce initiatives to lower the incidence of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads.
Key proposals include establishing a unified insurance premium for different vehicle types.
Furthermore, traffic violations recorded against vehicle owners could potentially affect their insurance costs.
A trial of the 'no insurance, no fuel' strategy will be initiated at select fuel stations.

items.title: Dalai Lama, office allotted bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi
points: The Centre has assigned a government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama.
This official accommodation aims to facilitate his visits to the national capital and provide comfort.
Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile have welcomed this arrangement as a supportive gesture towards their community.
Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011.

items.title: BSF constable dies by suicide in Arnia
points: In a tragic incident, Deva Nand Majhi, a young BSF constable stationed in Jammu and Kashmir, reportedly took his own life at a security camp.
The shocking event unfolded in the Arnia border region late Monday night when he allegedly utilized his service weapon.
Originally from Katsa in Bihar's Saran district, his remains have been sent to GMC Jammu's mortuary for autopsy.

items.title: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
points: Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake.
Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity.
The Border Roads Organisation defends its initiatives as critical for ensuring safety for pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra route.
Detractors warn that development could endanger local ecosystems, revealing a broader conflict between aspirations for growth and the need for environmental conservation.

items.title: Rijiju heaps praise on J&K Waqf Board led by BJP man
points: Union minister Kiren Rijiju praised the Jammu & Kashmir Waqf Board for its remarkable contributions across various sectors, particularly citing the development projects at the Hazratbal and Baba Reshi shrines.
Rijiju remarked that this waqf board serves as a role model for similar entities nationwide.
He also pledged to aid in skill development and training programs aimed at empowering the youth of Kashmir.

Indians among 13 killed in UAE bus-truck crash, 14 injured
points: In a heartbreaking incident in Ras Al Khaimah, thirteen lives were tragically lost, including several Indian nationals, as confirmed by the Indian consulate in Dubai.
A bus with 41 passengers collided with a parked truck, resulting in this devastating accident.
Emergency teams quickly responded, transporting the injured to local hospitals for care.
The consulate has established a helpline for those seeking further information and support regarding this unfortunate event.

'Udta Punjab' to 'Ubharta Punjab': BJP's Tarun Chugh pitches drug-free, gangs-free state
points: BJP leader Tarun Chugh has affirmed the alliance's determination to eliminate drug issues and reduce crime in Punjab.
Both BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are collaborating to tackle organized crime and restore public safety.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah has set an ambitious goal to achieve a drug-free Punjab by 2029, while also condemning the Aam Aadmi Party for failing to fulfill its drug eradication commitments.
